title: Schefflera

paragraphs.heading: Problems
paragraphs.text: In the home, plant diseases are very rarely a problem. Too much or too little water plus insects and mites are the main problems. Mealybugs, scale insects and mites are common pests of scheffleras. Root rot usually results from a soil mix that does not drain quickly or overly frequent watering.

paragraphs.heading: Problems
paragraphs.text: Dead areas form on leaves several days after exposure to excessive cold. Maintain temperatures above 50 °F. Do not place plants near air conditioning vents. Low light can cause leaf yellowing with spindly, weak stems. Leaf drop can be caused by excessive watering, by low humidity, or by chilling.

paragraphs.heading: Culture
paragraphs.text: Scheffleras prefer medium to bright light.

paragraphs.heading: Culture
paragraphs.text: Water scheffleras thoroughly, then let the soil dry to ½ inch deep before watering again. Never let a plant sit with water in its saucer.

paragraphs.heading: Culture
paragraphs.text: For more information see, HGIC 1459 Indoor Plants: Watering .

paragraphs.heading: Culture
paragraphs.text: Scheffleras prefer day temperatures between 65 and 75 °F. Nighttime temperatures should remain above 60 °F. Keep plants away from heat vents, radiators, open windows, and air conditioners. Hot or cold drafts will damage plants.

paragraphs.heading: Culture
paragraphs.text: Fertilize scheffleras regularly either with a water-soluble or a time-release houseplant fertilizer. Feed according to label directions. Plants growing in reduced light will need less frequent fertilization than plants growing in bright light.

paragraphs.heading: Culture
paragraphs.text: For more information see, HGIC 1450 Indoor Plants - Cleaning, Fertilizing, Containers & Light Requirements .

paragraphs.heading: Culture
paragraphs.text: Repot overcrowded plants at any season, using a general-purpose potting soil. To keep plants small, prune just above a leaf. Propagation is by seed, cuttings and air layering.

paragraphs.heading: Species & Cultivars
paragraphs.text: 'Amate' is a selection that has resistance to Alternaria leaf spot and spider mites. Its growth stays compact even in low light.
